sub_criteria.name: agentic system design
sub_criteria.text: Describes or evaluates an LLM agent that searches literature iteratively: query reformulation, multi-round search, citation-graph traversal, or crawling, rather than a single retrieval call.

sub_criteria.name: baseline search recall
sub_criteria.text: Reports how much of a target set a single-query or Boolean database search actually retrieves, giving a recall or coverage number the agentic systems can be measured against.

sub_criteria.name: benchmark construction
sub_criteria.text: Says how an evaluation set for literature search or deep research was built - where the gold papers came from, how queries were sampled, what the annotation protocol was.

sub_criteria.name: retrieval and reranking
sub_criteria.text: Contributes the retrieval or reranking method underneath: dense or hybrid retrieval, LLM rerankers, citation-aware ranking, or evidence on which component carries the gain.

sub_criteria.name: gains that fail
sub_criteria.text: Reports a replication failure, a weak or unbeaten baseline, benchmark leakage or construction that inflates scores, or a gain that vanishes under a different set or metric.

Our objective was to determine whether GenAI can assist with evidence synthesis by assessing its performance using its accuracy, error rates, and time savings compared to the traditional expert-driven approach. items.abstract_600: Higher education institutions require course leaders to continuously develop and refine academic modules to align with evolving educational standards and university guidelines. items.title: Beyond the Capability Boundary: Zeroth-Order Optimization for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
items.abstract_600: Self-evolving methods improve the capabilities of LLM agents by sampling trajectories from the underlying LLMs and learning from these trajectories. However, these methods struggle to learn beyond the inherent capability boundary of the agents, since the agents cannot sample correct trajectories on difficult examples for further improvements. items.title: Introduction to Large Language Models (LLMs) for dementia care and research
items.abstract_600: Introduction: Dementia is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that affects cognitive abilities including memory, reasoning, and communication skills, leading to gradual decline in daily activities and social engagement. In light of the recent advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, this paper aims to thoroughly analyse their potential applications and usefulness in dementia care and research. items.title: ResGAT: an improved graph neural network based on multi-head attention mechanism and residual network for paper classification
items.abstract_600: This work introduces an enhanced graph neural network model that integrates a multi-head attention mechanism and a residual network structure to dynamically allocate weights to various nodes within the graph, thereby enhancing its ability to handle complex multi-level citation relationships in academic papers.

items.abstract_600: This paper presents a multi-stage reranking system for repository-level code search, which leverages the vastly available commit histories of large open-source repositories to aid in bug fixing. We define the task of repository-level code search as retrieving the set of files from the current state of a code repository that are most relevant to addressing a user's question or bug. items.title: Fully Automated Scholarly Search for Biomedical Systematic Literature Reviews
items.abstract_600: Biomedical Systematic Literature Reviews (SLRs) play a fundamental role in evidence-informed healthcare and can serve as actionable insights for researchers and policy-making organizations in the field. items.abstract_600: BACKGROUND: The demand for mental health (MH) services in the community continues to exceed supply. items.title: Cited but Not Verified: Parsing and Evaluating Source Attribution in LLM Deep Research Agents
items.abstract_600: Large language models (LLMs) power deep research agents that synthesize information from hundreds of web sources into cited reports, yet these citations cannot be reliably verified. Current approaches either trust models to self-cite accurately, risking bias, or employ retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that does not validate source accessibility, relevance, or factual consistency. items.title: Investigating LLM Variability in Personalized Conversational Information Retrieval
items.abstract_600: Personalized Conversational Information Retrieval (CIR) has seen rapid progress in recent years, driven by the development of Large Language Models (LLMs). items.abstract_600: The recent contrastive language-image pre-training (CLIP) model has shown great success in a wide range of image-level tasks, revealing remarkable ability for learning powerful visual representations with rich semantics. An open and worthwhile problem is efficiently adapting such a strong model to the video domain and designing a robust video anomaly detector. items.title: Empowering Real-World: A Survey on the Technology, Practice, and Evaluation of LLM-driven Industry Agents
items.abstract_600: With the rise of large language models (LLMs), LLM agents capable of autonomous reasoning, planning, and executing complex tasks have become a frontier in artificial intelligence. items.abstract_600: As AI becomes part of everyday learning, many courses teach students to use it mainly as a productivity tool: how to prompt, search, summarize, write, code, and use tools more efficiently. We argue that AI education also needs a setting in which students learn to test AI and understand their own role in judging machine-produced knowledge. items.abstract_600: Abstract This paper presents a comprehensive review of the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Systematic Literature Reviews (SLRs). items.title: ReportBench: Evaluating Deep Research Agents via Academic Survey Tasks
items.abstract_600: The advent of Deep Research agents has substantially reduced the time required for conducting extensive research tasks. In this paper, we propose ReportBench, a systematic benchmark designed to evaluate the content quality of research reports generated by large language models (LLMs). items.abstract_600: Web-enabled LLM agents are changing how online information influences search outcomes. Existing Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) studies mainly focus on individual webpages.
